title: Mirror decoder vs HyperFormer adapter decoder under fixed embeddings
hypothesis: With identical fixed four-value task/layer/position embeddings, a shared-matrix Mirror decoder will use at least 30% fewer actual N=32 payload bytes than a generic HyperFormer MLP decoder while staying within 10% held-out adapter NRMSE.
physical_object: one shared 2x2 matrix W decoded with two fixed embedding angles
mirror_coordinate: fixed embedding c=(theta1,theta2,r1,r2); decoder returns R(theta1) W R(theta2)
logical_multiplicity: per-context logical adapters from the same embedding table
controls: generic HyperFormer MLP decoder 4->16->4 using identical fixed embeddings
affine full-matrix decoder using identical embeddings
rank-two shared-basis decoder using identical embeddings

task.fixed_embeddings: first two coordinates are angles; last two are zero for aligned contexts and nonzero for off-orbit contexts
task.teacher: aligned R(c0)W*R(c1), with 25% off-orbit contexts adding c2 D1+c3 D2

development.selection: choose MLP updates by dev held-out NRMSE; Mirror fits W on same training targets

paid_objects: same fixed embeddings for all methods

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror NRMSE <=1.10x generic MLP and actual N=32 payload <=0.70x generic MLP; report controls at matched embedding bytes.
failure_gate: Mirror misses either quality or byte gate, or affine/rank-two decoder matches it at equal/fewer bytes.
boundaries: Synthetic 2x2 adapter decoder screen, not Transformer fine-tuning.
Embeddings are fixed and byte-matched across decoders; no method may change code values.
The off-orbit subgroup is included to test private/general decoder needs.
